trino:position-deletes:v2.notes: Trino reads and writes position delete files for row-level DELETE, UPDATE, and MERGE operations when configured for merge-on-read mode

trino:position-deletes:v3.notes: Trino reads legacy position delete files on V3 tables and generates deletion vectors or positional delete files depending on configuration

trino:equality-deletes:v2.notes: Not supported as a write operation. Trino never produces equality delete files for DELETE/MERGE, writing positional deletes instead. Trino fully supports reading equality delete files written by other engines (such as Apache Flink) at query time
caveats: Write capability only: Trino does not produce equality delete files, but can read them

trino:equality-deletes:v3.notes: Equality deletes are replaced by deletion vectors in Iceberg V3; Trino does not write equality deletes

trino:merge-on-read:v2.notes: Trino supports merge-on-read for DELETE, UPDATE, and MERGE, creating position delete files at write time and merging them on read

trino:merge-on-read:v3.notes: Trino supports merge-on-read on V3 tables using Puffin deletion vectors

trino:copy-on-write:v2.notes: Measured against Trino 483: the connector has no copy-on-write mode. The delete_mode / update_mode table properties are rejected (INVALID_TABLE_PROPERTY) and all row-level mutations (DELETE, UPDATE, MERGE) are merge-on-read, writing positional delete files rather than rewriting data files
caveats: No copy-on-write write strategy; row-level mutations are always merge-on-read

trino:copy-on-write:v3.notes: Measured against Trino 483: no copy-on-write mode on V3 tables either; row-level mutations are merge-on-read (deletion vectors)
caveats: No copy-on-write write strategy; row-level mutations are always merge-on-read

trino:schema-evolution:v2.notes: Full schema evolution support via SQL: ADD COLUMN, DROP COLUMN, RENAME COLUMN, and altering column types without rewriting existing data files

trino:schema-evolution:v3.notes: Full schema evolution supported on V3 tables

trino:type-promotion:v2.notes: Trino supports Iceberg type widening via ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE (e.g., INT to BIGINT, FLOAT to DOUBLE, DECIMAL precision widening)

trino:type-promotion:v3.notes: Type promotion and widening supported on V3 tables

trino:column-default-values:v2.notes: Column default values are an Iceberg V3 metadata feature; not supported in format version 2

trino:column-default-values:v3.notes: Iceberg V3 spec introduces initial-default and write-default at the metadata level; Trino SQL DDL does not currently support declaring Iceberg column-level default values in CREATE TABLE or ALTER TABLE
caveats: Iceberg column defaults cannot be declared via Trino SQL DDL

trino:table-creation:v2.notes: Full DDL support: CREATE TABLE, CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS), with table properties for format_version, partitioning, location, and format (Parquet, ORC, Avro)

trino:table-creation:v3.notes: Supported via CREATE TABLE with format_version = 3

trino:hidden-partitioning:v2.notes: Full support for Iceberg partition transforms (year, month, day, hour, bucket, truncate) specified via the partitioning table property (e.g., partitioning = ARRAY['year(order_date)', 'bucket(account_id, 16)']); transparent partition pruning at query time

trino:hidden-partitioning:v3.notes: Hidden partitioning with single-source transforms supported on V3 tables

trino:partition-evolution:v2.notes: Partition spec evolution supported via ALTER TABLE ... SET PROPERTIES partitioning = ARRAY[...] without rewriting existing data; Trino queries prune partitions correctly across spec transitions

trino:partition-evolution:v3.notes: Partition evolution supported on V3 tables

trino:multi-arg-transforms:v2.notes: Multi-argument transforms are a V3 feature; not applicable to V2

trino:multi-arg-transforms:v3.notes: Trino's partitioning table property only supports single-column transforms (bucket, truncate, year, month, day, hour); multi-argument partition transforms cannot be declared in Trino DDL
caveats: Cannot be declared in Trino DDL; read path untested

trino:time-travel:v2.notes: Full SQL time-travel support via FOR TIMESTAMP AS OF and FOR VERSION AS OF clauses

trino:time-travel:v3.notes: Full time-travel support on V3 tables via FOR TIMESTAMP AS OF and FOR VERSION AS OF

trino:table-maintenance:v2.notes: Comprehensive table maintenance procedures: ALTER TABLE ... EXECUTE optimize for file compaction, system.expire_snapshots for snapshot cleanup, and system.remove_orphan_files for deleting unreferenced files

trino:table-maintenance:v3.notes: Table maintenance procedures (compaction, snapshot expiration, orphan file removal) operate on V3 tables

trino:branching-tagging:v2.notes: Read-only. Measured against Trino 483: branches and tags created by another engine are listed in the $refs metadata table and can be queried with FOR VERSION AS OF '<branch_or_tag>'. Trino cannot create them: there is no CREATE BRANCH / CREATE TAG DDL and no create_branch / create_tag table procedure (PROCEDURE_NOT_FOUND)
caveats: Trino reads/queries branches and tags but cannot create them

trino:branching-tagging:v3.notes: Read-only on V3 tables as well: Trino queries existing branches and tags via FOR VERSION AS OF but provides no DDL or procedure to create them
caveats: Trino reads/queries branches and tags but cannot create them

trino:read-support:v2.notes: High-performance vectorized read support across Parquet, ORC, and Avro data files with column projection, dynamic partition pruning, and predicate pushdown

trino:read-support:v3.notes: Full read support for Iceberg V3 tables including deletion vector resolution

trino:write-insert:v2.notes: Full support for INSERT INTO and CTAS append and overwrite operations into Iceberg tables

trino:write-insert:v3.notes: Full write support for V3 tables

trino:write-merge-update-delete:v2.notes: Full row-level mutation support via SQL MERGE INTO, UPDATE, and DELETE statements supporting both copy-on-write and merge-on-read modes

trino:write-merge-update-delete:v3.notes: Row-level mutations supported on V3 tables using deletion vectors

trino:catalog-integration:v2.notes: Extensive native catalog integrations including Iceberg REST catalog (Polaris, Unity, Lakekeeper), AWS Glue, Hive Metastore, Nessie, and JDBC catalogs

trino:catalog-integration:v3.notes: Catalog integrations work with V3 tables where the catalog supports Iceberg format version 3

trino:statistics:v2.notes: Trino reads and collects Iceberg column metrics (null counts, min/max values, NaN counts) from manifest files and Puffin files for cost-based optimization and scan pruning

trino:statistics:v3.notes: Column statistics and Puffin metrics supported for V3 tables

trino:bloom-filters:v2.notes: Trino supports file-level bloom filter generation and evaluation for ORC format via table properties (orc_bloom_filter_columns), and consumes statistics from Puffin files. Generic Parquet/Puffin table-level bloom filter indexing is in active development
caveats: Configured primarily for ORC files via orc_bloom_filter_columns

trino:bloom-filters:v3.notes: Puffin blob support is utilized for statistics; native table-level Puffin bloom filters remain partially implemented
caveats: Full table-level Puffin bloom filters still evolving

trino:aws-glue-catalog:v2.notes: Native first-class AWS Glue Data Catalog integration configured via iceberg.catalog.type=glue with IAM role authentication and credential management

trino:aws-glue-catalog:v3.notes: AWS Glue catalog integration supports V3 tables when enabled in catalog settings

trino:rest-catalog:v2.notes: First-class native Iceberg REST Catalog support configured via iceberg.catalog.type=rest with OAuth2 client credentials authentication, bearer tokens, and storage credential vending

trino:rest-catalog:v3.notes: REST catalog client supports V3 tables and endpoint capabilities as supported by the backing REST catalog server

trino:unity-catalog:v2.notes: Trino connects to Unity Catalog's Iceberg REST Catalog endpoint using OAuth2 authentication and vended storage credentials, or via the dedicated Trino Unity Catalog connector
caveats: Access via Iceberg REST endpoint requires Unity Catalog's Iceberg REST compatibility layer

trino:unity-catalog:v3.notes: Trino connects to Unity Catalog for V3 tables through the standard REST catalog protocol
caveats: Access is via Unity Catalog's Iceberg REST endpoint

trino:snowflake-horizon-catalog:v2.notes: Trino connects to Snowflake Horizon Catalog (built on Apache Polaris) via the Iceberg REST Catalog protocol with OAuth2 authentication and credential vending
caveats: Access is via generic Iceberg REST Catalog protocol

trino:snowflake-horizon-catalog:v3.notes: Trino connects to Snowflake Horizon Catalog for V3 tables through the generic REST catalog protocol
caveats: Access is via generic Iceberg REST Catalog protocol

trino:google-lakehouse:v2.notes: Google Lakehouse runtime catalog exposes a standard Iceberg REST catalog endpoint; Trino connects via the REST catalog client. Rated partial because this specific cloud pairing has not been measured end-to-end and Google credential vending specifics may vary
caveats: Inferred from generic Iceberg REST catalog support; not measured against Google Lakehouse specifically

trino:google-lakehouse:v3.notes: Google Lakehouse exposes an Iceberg REST catalog, and Trino speaks the REST catalog protocol. Rated partial because this pairing has not been measured end-to-end
caveats: Inferred from generic Iceberg REST catalog support; not measured against Google Lakehouse specifically

trino:variant-type:v2.notes: Variant type is a V3 feature; not applicable to V2

trino:variant-type:v3.notes: Trino maps native JSON / semi-structured types to Iceberg V3 binary Variant type, enabling predicate pushdown and efficient storage without schema flattening

trino:shredded-variant:v2.notes: Shredded Variant is a V3 feature; not applicable to V2

trino:shredded-variant:v3.notes: While basic Iceberg V3 Variant support is implemented in Trino, full query optimization and writing of shredded variant sub-columns is still evolving
caveats: Sub-column shredding write optimization is evolving in the Trino connector

trino:geometry-type:v2.notes: Geometry type is a V3 feature; not applicable to V2

trino:geometry-type:v3.notes: Trino provides first-class geospatial support (GEOMETRY and SPHERICAL_GEOGRAPHY) with spatial functions (ST_*) that map natively to Iceberg V3 Geo/Geometry types

trino:nanosecond-timestamps:v2.notes: Nanosecond timestamps are a V3 feature; not applicable to V2

trino:nanosecond-timestamps:v3.notes: Trino natively supports TIMESTAMP(9) and TIMESTAMP(9) WITH TIME ZONE, mapping directly to Iceberg V3 nanosecond precision timestamp and timestamptz columns

trino:unknown-type:v2.notes: Unknown type is a V3 feature; not available in format version 2

trino:unknown-type:v3.notes: Measured against Trino 483: reading a V3 table that has an Iceberg unknown-type column fails with NOT_SUPPORTED ("Cannot convert from Iceberg type 'unknown' (UNKNOWN) to Trino type"). Trino cannot declare or query the unknown type
caveats: V3-only feature; Trino cannot map the Iceberg unknown type

trino:lineage:v2.notes: Row Lineage is a V3 feature; not applicable to V2

trino:lineage:v3.notes: Trino supports Iceberg V3 row lineage metadata tracking for data provenance, auditability, and change tracking

trino:deletion-vectors:v2.notes: Deletion vectors are a V3 feature; not applicable to Iceberg V2

trino:deletion-vectors:v3.notes: Trino supports Iceberg V3 Puffin-format Deletion Vectors for efficient row-level deletion and merge-on-read operations without creating separate positional delete files for every commit
